predictions.description: The founder says clips must be genuinely good and that this is the whole product, but no definition, selection method, examples, or editorial rules are given.
There is no measurable success condition for clip quality, despite clip quality being described as the core product.
There is no stated way to test or prove that suggested clips are genuinely good rather than random chunks.
Same-evening and feel fast enough are not quantified: no SLA, timezone, hours-from-upload, or dependence on episode length is specified.
Desired same-evening posting lacks a measurable latency or completion-rate target for forty-to-ninety-minute episodes.
It is unclear whether the product only suggests or exports clips, or also posts to social networks; clip media type, duration, captions, and platforms are unspecified.
Hosting is decided as the same cloud provider as another project, but the provider, regions, services, and limits are not identified.
The product is constrained to an existing unnamed cloud provider; whether that provider can host transcription and clip generation remains unresolved.
Suitability of the existing cloud provider for audio processing and same-evening turnaround is assumed by the hosting decision without supporting evidence in the sources.
Ten episodes included and wait until the next month do not specify calendar month versus rolling period, timezone, what counts as an episode, or queue/notification behavior while waiting.
Under five thousand listeners an episode could mean downloads, unique listeners, subscribers, or another metric, so the target-user boundary is unclear.
Short clips are required and random thirty-second chunks are rejected, but no accepted duration range is given.
Hard wait on the eleventh episode with no overage is visible and may block same-evening posting for heavier publishers, but no mitigation or expected publishing cadence is stated.
Accepted audio formats, file-size limits, channel/layout constraints, and handling of episodes outside forty to ninety minutes are not stated.
Transcription is required, but accuracy target, speaker labels, timestamps, human review, and provider versus in-house method are absent.
Pricing and quota are declared settled, but the sources contain no evidence that nineteen euro and ten episodes fit the stated solo-podcaster target.
Same-evening turnaround for forty-to-ninety-minute audio is a material latency risk, and no capacity, cost, or failure-mode control is visible against the mandated unspecified cloud.
